introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, "Answer all Questions"): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown: Two protons A and B each of mass $1.70\times10^{-27}\ \mathrm{kg}$ are separated by a distance $a$ of $1.00\times10^{-13}\ \mathrm{m}$.
incertitudes: Question 3 : aucune constante n'est donnée par le sujet ; e = 1,60 x 10^-19 C, 1/(4 pi epsilon_0) = 8,99 x 10^9 et G = 6,67 x 10^-11 sont retenues et dites dans le corrigé. La masse du proton imprimée (1,70 x 10^-27 kg) est utilisée telle quelle (la valeur courante est 1,67 x 10^-27 kg). Question 3 : le sujet imprime « (6 marks) » une seule fois, en fin de question ; `points` de l'exercice vaut 6, aucune sous-question ne porte de points.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a diagram showing the forces acting on the protons.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Diagram (to be drawn by the candidate).** Draw the two protons as small circles labelled A and B on a horizontal line, a distance $a$ apart. Each proton is acted on by **two forces**, drawn as arrows from its centre:

- the **electrostatic force $F_e$**, **repulsive** (both charges are positive): on A it points to the left, away from B; on B it points to the right, away from A;
- the **gravitational force $F_g$**, **attractive**: on A it points to the right, towards B; on B it points to the left, towards A.

The two forces on A are in opposite directions, and the force on A is equal and opposite to the same kind of force on B (Newton's third law): $F_e$ on A $= F_e$ on B, and $F_g$ on A $= F_g$ on B. The arrows for $F_e$ must be drawn much longer than those for $F_g$ (the diagram cannot be to scale, since $F_e/F_g\approx10^{36}$); the net force on each proton is repulsive.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the ratio of the electric force to the gravitational force between the protons. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Constants used (no data sheet is printed): $e = 1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 8.99\times10^{9}\ \mathrm{N\,m^2\,C^{-2}}$, $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}\ \mathrm{N\,m^2\,kg^{-2}}$.

Electric force (Coulomb's law):
$$F_e = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{e^2}{a^2} = \frac{8.99\times10^{9}\times(1.60\times10^{-19})^2}{(1.00\times10^{-13})^2} = 2.30\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{N}$$

Gravitational force (Newton's law of gravitation):
$$F_g = \frac{G m^2}{a^2} = \frac{6.67\times10^{-11}\times(1.70\times10^{-27})^2}{(1.00\times10^{-13})^2} = 1.93\times10^{-38}\ \mathrm{N}$$

Ratio:
$$\frac{F_e}{F_g} = \frac{2.30\times10^{-2}}{1.93\times10^{-38}} = 1.19\times10^{36}$$

**$F_e/F_g \approx 1.2\times10^{36}$.** The separation $a$ cancels in the ratio (both forces vary as $1/a^2$): the electric repulsion is about $10^{36}$ times stronger than the gravitational attraction, so gravity is negligible between charged particles.
